page: OVHcloud r3-256 is a memory-optimized cloud instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. With a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio, the environment operates without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring non-contended execution per core. Hardware caching includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache.

Resource allocation is centered around memory capacity, offering 256 GB of system RAM at an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8 GB per vCPU). The server also integrates 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 8 Gbps. It does not include GPU acceleration or bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Synthetic testing demonstrates strong multi-threaded performance and high memory bandwidth, ranking in the top 25% across stress-ng multi-core tests, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and large-block memory read and write metrics. In memory-centric key-value testing, the configuration sustained 75.95 million Redis SET operations per second alongside top-tier database operation scores. Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects average performance consistent with its 2.3 GHz clock frequency.

By dedicating entire physical CPU cores to substantial RAM and fast local NVMe storage, the r3-256 offers balanced compute density and qualitative resource efficiency for large in-memory footprints. The server is well configured for in-memory databases, Redis caches, large-scale relational database management systems, data processing pipelines, and multi-threaded compilation workloads.
description: OVHcloud r3-256 is a memory-optimized virtual instance equipped with 32 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. Designed for data-heavy workloads, it pairs 32 non-threaded vCPUs with 256 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 RAM-to-CPU ratio. Storage is provided locally via a 400 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no GPU acceleration. Benchmark assessments reveal strong multi-core computational throughput and top-tier memory bandwidth, reflected in high marks for Redis SET operations and PassMark database metrics, while single-core performance remains average. The dedicated core architecture avoids thread contention, offering predictable multi-threaded performance. Consequently, the r3-256 delivers strong resource efficiency for memory-intensive applications, including Redis caching tiers, relational database systems, in-memory analytics, and parallel data processing workloads.
